newsitem.title: USA: TWA seeks code-share with Royal Jordanian.
newsitem.headline: TWA seeks code-share with Royal Jordanian.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc said Monday it filed an application with the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT), seeking approval of code-share service with Royal Jordanian Airline.

The agreement calls for the joint coding of TWA's domestic flights between seven U.S. cities and John F. Kennedy Airport in New York and Royal Jordanian's direct flights between JFK, Amsterdam and Amman, Jordan.
Service is expected to begin in late summer, TWA said.
TWA's seven cities to be included in the service are Chicago, Washington, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Miami, Detroit and St. Louis, TWA's hub. Additional cities may be added later, it added.

"Our code-share agreement and filing with the DOT pave the way for a dramatic new alliance for TWA that brings the exciting business and pleasure destinations of Amman and Amsterdam to our customers," Gerald Gitner, chairman, said in a statement.

Separately, TWA said it named Blanche Touhill, chancellor of the University of Missouri-St. Louis, and retired Gen. Merrill "Tony" McPeak, former chief of staff of the U.S. Air Force, to its board of directors.
They assume the seats held by Jewel Lafontant-Mankarious and Lawrence Roos, both of whom will retire effective with the annual meeting on May 29.
